summary: CCC-built 1936 L-4 lookout in Lewis & Clark National Forest, lowered off its pole in 1999 and rebuilt on a ground foundation as a seasonal rental.

facts.design: L-4 cab, 14x14 ft, originally on a 50-foot pole tower with catwalk; now on a short ground foundation
facts.status_note: relocated from a 50-foot pole tower to a ground-level foundation in 1999

staffing.status: unstaffed since the late 20th century; exact end date disputed between sources

access.note: seasonal rental via recreation.gov, June 1 - November 30; high-clearance vehicle recommended for final 2 miles

visit.trail_note: 2 miles of rough, rocky road; muddy/slippery when wet

facts.agency: U.S. Forest Service - Lewis & Clark National Forest

events.note: built by the Civilian Conservation Corps as an L-4 cab on a 50-foot pole tower
cab removed from the pole tower after becoming unstable and placed on the ground for restoration
rededicated in July 2005 and placed in the recreation rental program as a ground facility
registered on the National Historic Lookout Register, July 31, 2005

evidence.supports: 1936 build, L-4 cab on 50-ft pole, active until 1999, lowered for restoration, rededicated July 2005
evidence.quote: The 14'x14' L-4 cab with catwalk was originally placed on a 50' pole tower in 1936. Monument Peak Lookout in the Lewis & Clark National Forest remained active until 1999 when it became unstable and the cab was placed on the ground for restoration. The lookout was rededicated in July 2005

evidence.supports: 1936 CCC build, unused since 1970s, 1999 removal and restoration, seasonal rental dates, road/access details, cabin facilities, occupancy limit
evidence.quote: The lookout, built in 1936 by the Civilian Conservation Corps, is perched atop Monument Peak... The lookout was once used to spot forest fires but was left unused since the 1970s. In 1999, the lookout was removed from its 50 foot pole, restored and placed on a short, solid foundation for public rental use. A high clearance vehicle is recommended, as the 2 miles of road leading up to the cabin are rough and rocky. During wet conditions the entie road may be muddy and often times slippery. The Lookout/Cabin is avaialble for rental between June 1 and Novemebr 30. The rustic lookout has two beds with mattresses, two propane lanterns, a table and chairs and a propane cooking stove. A vault toilet is about 100 feet from the structure. No water, electricity or plumbing is available. The cabin sleeps two people, however, two additional tents are allowed at the site (accommodating another four people). The whole facility can only provide enough room and service for six people total.

evidence.supports: 50-foot pole tower with L-4 cab, only surviving example of its type in Montana, abandoned since the 1970s
evidence.quote: This 50' pole tower with L-4 cab, built in 1936, was the only existing example of its type left in Montana. Abandoned since the 1970's, the cab was lowered to the ground in 1999

resolved_conflicts.explanation: NHLR states the lookout remained active until 1999 when it became unstable, while recreation.gov and firelookout.com both say it was left unused/abandoned since the 1970s; could not resolve which is correct from sources checked

notes_for_editor: Conflict between NHLR (active until 1999) and recreation.gov/firelookout.com (unused since the 1970s) noted in the story and in resolved_conflicts; genuinely unresolved from the sources checked here.
